scope: Bounded graph from one caller-owned scanned root: nonstatic Java-declared reference fields, inherited fields and object-array elements; primitive arrays are leaves.
exclusions: All reference fields declared by the exact bootstrap java/lang/ref/Reference, before slot load
Injected/VM-only fields and Class metadata edges
Arbitrary VM root and retained-size analysis
protocol: Use existing verified native VMoperation, actual safepoint-aware Heap_lock and VMThread callback; same exact-profile and collector admission as heap_iteration.

Caller root is refreshed from its scanned slot only at the actual safepoint; strong declared edges are copied while mutators are stopped. No discovered oop is published as a new root or retained after the callback.

Fixed node/edge/class/hash/label buffers are allocated before the callback. Array/Symbol/oop decoding helpers are prewarmed on the caller; no C++ allocation, JavaCalls, callbacks or first-use C++ static guard inside traversal.
Only copied IDs, labels, kind/length and field/index records survive the safepoint; class and oop identity dedup uses exact pointer equality within that operation.
Well-known bootstrap Reference identity is cached only for the audited JVM lifetime and its mirror is locally retained for each capture. Application class identity is never cached between captures.

All Reference-declared reference fields are conservatively excluded, including queue/next/discovered. This deliberately narrower scope avoids assuming physical oop-map edges are ordinary strong Java fields.
Symbol labels preserve raw modified UTF-8 bytes. Java String conversion is not applied inside VMThread.
All six budgets explicitly mark partial results. C++ materialization happens after the safepoint and preserves original bad_alloc including derived exceptions.
